Hello,

I am facing an issue in getting R mapreduce work on my distributed cluster.
 
I have a 11 node cluster. (1 NN, 1 SNN, 1 JT, 8 WN)
 
I have installed R, rhdfs and rmr2 on all the nodes. I followed below steps to install.
 
R Installation
  1. ./configure --prefix=/opt/hadoop/R --enable-R-shlib --with-readline=no --with-x=no
  2. make
  3. make install
  4. Added /opt/hadoop/R/bin to PATH in ~/.bash_profile file

RHadoop Installation

  1. R CMD javareconf JAVA=/opt/jdk1.6.0_32x64/bin/java JAVA_HOME=/opt/jdk1.6.0_32x64 JAVAC=/opt/jdk1.6.0_32x64/bin/javac JAR=/opt/jdk1.6.0_32x64/bin/jar JAVAH=/opt/jdk1.6.0_32x64/bin/javah

  6. install.packages(c( 'RJSONIO', 'itertools', 'digest','functional', 'stringr', 'plyr'))
  7. R CMD INSTALL Rcpp_0.10.4.tar.gz
  8. R CMD INSTALL quickcheck_1.0.tar.gz
  9. R CMD INSTALL reshape2_1.2.2.tar.gz
  10. R CMD INSTALL rmr2_2.0.2.tar.gz

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#906] Issue with mapreduce function in distributed cluster
parts: Something like this normally is due to permission issues or environment settings. When you say "I have Rscript available on all the nodes" you should also make sure that that is true for all users, but this line
1. Added /opt/hadoop/R/bin to PATH in ~/.bash_profile file

is obviously user specific. What happens is that mapreduce jobs run usually as a special hadoop user for which ~ expands to a different path. Our scripts operate directly on /etc/profile, but there may be other ways to achieve the same result. I hope this helps

Antonio

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#909] Re: Issue with mapreduce function in distributed cluster
parts:
On Fri, Jul 26, 2013 at 9:50 AM, Ravi <ravi.mam...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks for the reply Antonio.
 
Coud you please elaborate?
 
I have verified with the user account that I use accross my cluster.
That doesn't help because hadoop doesn't use that account to run mapreduce jobs, at least in a number of instances I worked with.

Also, as you mentioned in one of the posts, I added the PATH to backend parameters in the mapreduce function call.
 
backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(cmdenv="PATH=/opt/hadoop/R/bin ")
I wouldn't recommend to use this approach. Now you've removed /bin from the PATH. That's not going to fly. You need to extend the PATH with that entry and you can't do that with cmdenv
I also tried Sys.setenv(PATH="/opt/hadoop/R/bin")

Again when you set things, you need to ask yourself in what environment (user, machine). Again, is you have access to /etc/profile, I would set the PATH there. And don't erase what's already set, add a line such as

export PATH=$PATH:/opt/hadoop/R/bin

Antonio
 
 
Thanks
Ravi
